notes: The tutorial title/URL is inferred; no official id was given.
Arduino MKR Zero is not in the catalogue, so it is a new part type (MKR header pins plus USB).
The catalogue already has grove-relay, so it is used for the Grove Relay even though the parts list said 'None'.

Grove cables are not in the catalogue. I added a grove-cable connector type (a and b are one node). The carrier and hub Grove ports are 'socket' kind, so the cable plug ends are given kind 'ball' as the nearest compatible stand-in for a plug that snaps into a socket.

The carrier has one generic 'grove' port, not separate A0/D0/D1/TWI ports. The pin assignment (A0 moisture, D0 water, D1 relay, TWI via I2C hub) comes from the text, so the three sensor cables and the TWI cable all use port 'grove'.
Grove module connectors are not named ports. The joined edge to a module therefore has no port, and the electrical edge names the signal port (SIG or SCL).

The power section follows the 'next step' diagram, which I could not see. It is reconstructed from the text: the 12V supply goes to the carrier VIN/GND screw block (modelled as the carrier 'VCC' and 'GND' ports) and to relay COM. The pump goes between relay NO and GND.

The carrier VCC and GND ports are pin-kind and cannot take a wire-end or the supply's DC port as a 'joined' edge. The screw-terminal clamps on the carrier are therefore 'contact' plus 'electrical' edges. The relay and pump screw terminals keep 'joined' edges.
The wall-wart has a single 'DC' port, so the supply's ground return is not modelled separately.

The water sensor hack uses two solid wires of different lengths soldered to two non-adjacent tinned bars. They are modelled as jumper-wire parts joined to the sensor. Their free ends go into the tank.
The Arduino IDE is software only, so it is represented only by the laptop on the USB cable.
The moisture sensor probe goes in the soil and the water sensor wires go in the tank. These are physical placements and are not graph edges.
The Gmail, Google Calendar and Google Drive connectors need authorization (claude.ai connector settings). They are unavailable in this non-interactive session. This task did not need them.
